messages:
Anya: Heads-up — spotted a p99 regression on chat streaming when we force microbatch size <= 4 and the KV cache is cold. Repro on canary with the new kernel picker.
Mike: ugh, can you paste the run id / simple repro?
Anya: run id `canary-2026-03-18-08`. Steps: 1) flush kvcache, 2) send 1k short chat requests (avg 40 tokens), 3) set mbsize=4 streaming. p95 ok, p99 jumps ~230ms.
Luis: roughly where in the tail is the time going? token generation or initial handshake?
Anya: initial token delay + first-kernel-latency. Trace shows a ~180ms block inside `choose_kernel()` then a KV miss penalty ~40ms.
Sasha: that sounds like kernel selection is doing a heavyweight probe on small batches. We changed heuristics last week to prefer fused kernels for short seqs. Could be expensive decision path.
Oliver: repro logs?
Anya: pasted sample trace: ```
[2026-03-18T08:12:01Z] request=abc123 stage=queue wait_ms=12
[2026-03-18T08:12:01Z] request=abc123 stage=kernel_choice start
[2026-03-18T08:12:01Z] kernel_probe model=redwood-1 speed_est_ms=168
[2026-03-18T08:12:01Z] request=abc123 stage=kv_lookup miss
[2026-03-18T08:12:01Z] kv_fetch_ms=41
[2026-03-18T08:12:01Z] request=abc123 stage=emit_token start
```
Mike: that `kernel_probe` number is suspiciously high. Maybe we're doing a synchronous microbenchmark per-request for tiny mbsize. Should be amortized.
Luis: Agreed. We intended to cache kernel choice per-model+seqlen+hw-ticks but if mbsize small and streaming profile varies per-request we might be invalidating too often.
Sasha: can we try two quick experiments: (A) pin kernel choice after first decision for N seconds, (B) increase mbsize to 8 and re-run?
Anya: started (A) now — toggled `kernel_pin_ttl=5s` on canary, same load. Perf logs posted by perf-bot.
perf-bot: [perf report] canary-2026-03-18-08 kernel_pin_ttl=5s => p99 reduced from 230ms to 95ms, p95 steady. Summary: kernel probe was the dominant tail contributor. Link: https://perf.internal/runs/canary-2026-03-18-08
Mike: promising. What about KV miss impact? If kernel pinning reduces probe, KV miss still adds 40ms but p99 improved, so kernel was main culprit.
Luis: but pinning has tradeoffs — could misselect for longer sequences and harm throughput. Need to validate across seqlen distribution.
Sasha: for (B) I re-ran with mbsize=8 streaming (no kernel pin). p99 down to 110ms, but throughput decreased 8% due to increased per-batch overhead for small requests.
Oliver: so tradeoff space: smaller mbsize -> higher probe frequency (worse tail) but higher throughput density for streaming; larger mbsize -> lower tail but less responsiveness per-client.
Anya: also saw a regression when we fallback to quantized kernels: fallback path does a slow compatibility check, adds ~70ms occasionally. Might be happening on cold kernel cache.
Mike: action items: 1) short-term: enable `kernel_pin_ttl=5s` for streaming endpoints with mbsize<=4, test for regressions on long seqs. 2) mid-term: change kernel picker to async probe + future cache (don't block request on probe). 3) investigate kv prefetch on first token for chat streams.
Luis: + add a metric for "kernel_probe_count_per_request" and attach to p99 alert to catch re-occurrence.
Sasha: I'll run regression matrix across seqlen buckets [8,64,256] and mbsize [2,4,8,16] against dedicated kernel pin and async probe branch.
Oliver: FYI I saw a related postmortem note from last year — we tried pinning and had a rare correctness blip with fused kernels. Need correctness tests in the canary.
Anya: noted — will add end-to-end convo tests for fused vs fallback kernels before enabling pin globally.
perf-bot: test runner queued: `e2e-fused-kernel-check` on canary-2026-03-18-08, ETA 20m.
Mike: thanks. small wins first: roll kernel_pin_ttl on low-risk streaming routes, measure p99 and error rates for 24h.
Sasha: I'll post the regression matrix results here when ready. Expected finish ~2h. :clock1:
Anya: cool. I'll keep monitoring the canary trace and KV warmup scripts. If anyone wants to pair on async probe design ping me.
Oliver: pinged.
Mike: awesome work team.
